keys.Description: An SSH server package or unit exists on the host.
The SSH service is running or socket-activated.
A telnet server package, unit or inetd entry exists on the host.
A telnet server would accept a connection from off the host (active unit or listening socket unit, non-loopback).
Listening TCP/UDP sockets with proto, address, port, inode, pid and executable.
How sshd options were obtained - G, T or parse.
Whether per-persona (Match) values were collected; false means options hold global values only.
Effective PermitRootLogin value (daemon-reported versus parsed files).
OpenSSH version reported by sshd -V (major.minor); absent when it could not be read.
Effective MaxAuthTries (daemon-reported versus parsed files).
Effective ClientAliveInterval in seconds (daemon-reported versus parsed files); 0 disables the keepalive.
Effective ClientAliveCountMax (daemon-reported versus parsed files).
Effective Banner path, or none for sshd's default of no pre-auth banner.
Every Include the sshd_config parse followed, in expansion order - path, line, depth.
Whether the file named by sshd's Banner exists; false when Banner is none.
Whether the file named by sshd's Banner has non-whitespace content.
Whether /etc/issue has non-whitespace content.
Whether /etc/issue announces the distribution or release (an issue escape or the distro name).
Permission bits of /etc/issue; 0 when the file is absent.
Whether /etc/issue.net has non-whitespace content.
Whether /etc/issue.net announces the distribution or release (an issue escape or the distro name).
Permission bits of /etc/issue.net; 0 when the file is absent.
Whether /etc/motd has non-whitespace content.
Permission bits of /etc/motd; 0 when the file is absent.
Inventory of /etc/update-motd.d entries - name and whether each is executable.
Whether /etc/update-motd.d holds at least one executable script.
Presence and permission facts of /etc/securetty (absent on RHEL 8+ and Debian-family).
Non-comment lines of /etc/securetty. A sibling leaf, not a member of files.etc_securetty, because every leaf under facts is an envelope of its own.
Permission bits of /etc/passwd as an integer (e.g. 420 for 0644).
Owner uid of /etc/passwd.
Group gid of /etc/passwd.
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/passwd.
Group name for the gid of /etc/passwd from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/passwd include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/passwd include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/passwd include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/passwd include write (derived from mode).
Access ACL entries of /etc/passwd in setfacl form with numeric ids (user::rw-, user:1000:rw-, group::r--, mask::rw-, other::r--); empty when no ACL is set.
Permission bits of /etc/shadow as an integer (e.g. 256 for 0400).
Owner uid of /etc/shadow.
Group gid of /etc/shadow.
Group name for the gid of /etc/shadow from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/shadow include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/shadow include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/shadow include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/shadow include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/shadow.
Access ACL entries of /etc/shadow in setfacl form with numeric ids (user::rw-, user:1000:rw-, group::r--, mask::rw-, other::r--); empty when no ACL is set.
Permission bits of /etc/hosts as an integer (e.g. 384 for 0600).
Owner uid of /etc/hosts.
Group gid of /etc/hosts.
Group name for the gid of /etc/hosts from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/hosts include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/hosts include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/hosts include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/hosts include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/hosts.
Permission bits of /etc/services as an integer (e.g. 384 for 0600).
Owner uid of /etc/services.
Group gid of /etc/services.
Group name for the gid of /etc/services from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/services include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/services include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/services include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/services include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/services.
Permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd as an integer (e.g. 384 for 0600).
Owner uid of /etc/hosts.lpd.
Group gid of /etc/hosts.lpd.
Group name for the gid of /etc/hosts.lpd from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/hosts.lpd.
One row per /etc/passwd account with its home path, interactive flag, and the home's stat status, mode, ownership match, group/other write bits and whether it sits on a remote filesystem.
System-scope and per-home shell environment files that exist, with path, scope, owning account, mode, owner match, group/other write bits and whether the file is a symlink.
.rhosts and .shosts files under interactive homes, as derived flags only - owning account match, whether a wildcard "+" entry is present and the non-comment entry count, never the file body.
Permission bits of /root as an integer (e.g. 448 for 0700).
Owner uid of /root.
Group gid of /root.
Whether the group permission bits of /root include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /root include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /root.
Permission bits of /etc/hosts.equiv as an integer; absent when the file does not exist.
Owner uid of /etc/hosts.equiv; absent when the file does not exist.
Non-comment lines of /etc/hosts.equiv; an OK empty list when the file does not exist, since a host-based trust file that is absent grants no trust.
Every node one and two levels under /dev, each with name, path, kind, serving filesystem type, mode and owner uid; bounded and marked truncated if the bound is hit.
The subset of /dev entries that are regular files served by the /dev mount itself (not a deeper tmpfs such as /dev/shm) - the stale or planted files U-26 flags.
SysV init scripts and systemd unit files under the startup roots, each with path, mode, owner, group, the group/other-writable flags and is_symlink - the enabled-unit symlinks U-17 filters out.
The startup-script directories themselves (/etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system, the rcN.d dirs), each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags.
The rsyslog and syslog-ng configuration files, each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags.
The systemd-journald configuration files, each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags.
Mode bits of /etc/inetd.conf (0o7777); absent when the file does not exist, as it does not on either stock family.
Owner uid of /etc/inetd.conf; absent when the file does not exist.
Whether /etc/inetd.conf is group-writable; absent when the file does not exist.
Whether /etc/inetd.conf is world-readable; absent when the file does not exist.
Mode bits of /etc/xinetd.conf (0o7777); absent when the file does not exist.
Owner uid of /etc/xinetd.conf; absent when the file does not exist.
The /etc/xinetd.d fragment files, each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags; an ok empty list when the directory holds none.
PASS_MAX_DAYS - persisted in login.defs, effective as the maximum over existing accounts' shadow fields.
PASS_MIN_DAYS - persisted in login.defs, effective as the minimum over existing accounts' shadow fields.
PASS_MIN_LEN from login.defs (ignored by PAM when pwquality is present; stage 2 adds the pwquality side).
PASS_WARN_AGE - persisted in login.defs, effective as the minimum warn field over existing accounts' shadow rows.
UID_MIN from login.defs, the lowest uid of a regular (non-system) account.
SYS_UID_MAX from login.defs, the highest uid useradd assigns to a system account.
SHA_CRYPT_MIN_ROUNDS from login.defs.
UMASK from login.defs, verbatim (a mask, not a number).
HOME_MODE from login.defs, verbatim.
ENCRYPT_METHOD from login.defs, verbatim (SHA512, YESCRYPT, ...); PAM may override it.
ENV_SUPATH from login.defs, verbatim (the PATH= assignment for root logins).
ENV_PATH from login.defs, verbatim (the PATH= assignment for other logins).

Local accounts in /etc/passwd order with name, uid, gid, home, shell, system (0 < uid < UID_MIN, where UID_MIN is login.defs' value or 1000 when it is unset or unreadable; nobody is not a system account), shadowed (passwd field is x), uid_duplicate, name_duplicate, shell_valid (shell listed in /etc/shells) and, when /etc/shadow was read or does not exist, password_status (hashed | locked | nopass | noshadow), locked, hash_algo ("$6$"-style id, "legacy" for a hash without one, "" when there is no hash) and the ageing fields; no hashes. Ageing fields are -1 when the shadow field is empty, and uid/gid are -1 when the passwd field is unparsable.

The login shells listed in /etc/shells, in file order; when the file does not exist, the libc default (/bin/sh, /bin/csh) with a reason saying so; carries the read's status when the file is unreadable.
Lines of /etc/passwd and /etc/group that could not be parsed as an account or group (too few fields, a non-numeric uid or gid); a mangled file must not read as a clean host.
Local groups in /etc/group order with name, gid, members (the listed secondary members, duplicates removed), member_count and gid_duplicate.

Accounts whose primary gid names no group in /etc/group, as name and gid in /etc/passwd order; [] when every primary group exists; carries the read's status when /etc/passwd or /etc/group is unreadable.

Members of the administrative groups root, wheel, sudo and admin other than the root account itself - name, group and via (primary when the account's gid is the group's, secondary when listed in /etc/group) - in /etc/group order, primary members before secondary ones.

Whether /etc/shadow exists and every /etc/passwd entry defers to it (password field x); a false names the first account that does not; carries the read's status when /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd is unreadable.
The sources on the passwd line of /etc/nsswitch.conf, in order, with bracketed actions removed; absent when the file or the line is missing (glibc then resolves from files).
The sources on the group line of /etc/nsswitch.conf, in order, with bracketed actions removed; absent when the file or the line is missing.

Whether the passwd or group database names a remote source in use: any source other than files, compat, systemd or db, where sss counts only when /etc/sssd/sssd.conf exists (compat's NIS + entries are not detected); account controls judged on the local files report WARN while this is true (spec section 7.3).

The expanded PAM stacks of login, sshd, su, sudo, passwd and other (those whose /etc/pam.d file exists) - service, type, control, module, args, path, line - with @include, include and substack spliced where they stand and authselect's symlinks resolved by name into /etc/authselect, never by following the link. Backslash line continuation and a pam.conf-only host are not handled.
How the stacks are generated - authselect (a managed file is a symlink into /etc/authselect), pam-auth-update (the marker in common-auth) or manual.

Whether every include of every published service was read; a false names the first unreadable, missing, undeclared, looping or too-deep include in its reason, and every derived pam.* value then carries error instead of a number.
pam_pwquality.so is stacked in passwd's password stack with a control field other than optional; a false names why. Every other pam.pwquality.* key is absent while this is false.
The local_users_only argument or setting is present, so pwquality skips accounts that are not in /etc/passwd.
Effective minlen - the default 8, then pwquality.conf, then pwquality.conf.d/*.conf in name order, then the module arguments, each overriding the last.
Effective minclass (default 0), resolved like minlen.
Effective dcredit (default 0), resolved like minlen; a negative value is a minimum count of digits.
Effective ucredit (default 0), resolved like minlen.
Effective lcredit (default 0), resolved like minlen.
Effective ocredit (default 0), resolved like minlen.
The character classes a new password must contain - the larger of minclass and the number of credits set to -1 or lower.
enforce_for_root is set in a conf file or as a module argument.

The hashing argument on pam_unix.so in passwd's password stack (md5, bigcrypt, sha256, sha512, blowfish, gost_yescrypt or yescrypt); empty when none is given and login.defs ENCRYPT_METHOD decides; absent when the stack has no pam_unix line.

How many previous passwords a new one is checked against - remember= on pam_pwhistory.so (argument, else pwhistory.conf, else the module default 10) or on pam_unix.so; absent when neither module sets it.

Every existing login-facing service (login, sshd) stacks pam_faillock.so with preauth and with authfail in its auth phase and, in its account phase, pam_faillock.so, or an authsucc line in the auth phase; a false names the first service that does not. The other pam.faillock.* keys are absent while this is false.

Effective deny - the default 3, then faillock.conf, then the preauth arguments, then the authfail arguments; 0 disables the lockout. What is published is the merge of faillock.conf, the preauth arguments and the authfail arguments, the authfail line applied last; when the two lines disagree pam.faillock.enabled says so in its reason. A conf= argument naming another file is not handled.
Effective unlock_time in seconds (default 600), resolved like deny; 0 means the account stays locked until an administrator releases it.
Effective fail_interval in seconds (default 900), resolved like deny.
even_deny_root is set in faillock.conf or as a module argument (with or without a value), or root_unlock_time is set, which implies it.
Effective root_unlock_time in seconds, resolved like deny; unlock_time when not set.
su's auth stack has a pam_wheel.so line whose control field is required or requisite and whose arguments do not include deny, so only the wheel group (or group=) may use su; a false names why.
The control field of the first pam_wheel.so line in su's auth stack; absent when there is none.
The group pam_wheel.so restricts su to - its group= argument, or wheel; absent when there is no pam_wheel line.
The arguments of that pam_wheel.so line; absent when there is none.
pam_umask.so is in the session stack of login (else sshd, else other), which applies a umask where /etc/profile never runs.
The arguments of the first pam_umask.so session line; absent when the module is not stacked.
login's auth stack has a pam_securetty.so line (any control), so /etc/securetty is consulted for root logins on a console; absent when there is no login service.
Container runtime detected from filesystem markers (none, docker, podman, lxc, other); the same value the run header carries.
Whether /run/systemd/system exists, so unit state can be asked of systemd.
Effective TMOUT in seconds from the system profile files; 0 when unset (bash reads 0 as no timeout).
Whether the winning TMOUT is exported so child login shells inherit it.
Whether TMOUT is made readonly so a user cannot unset it.
Every TMOUT assignment - path, line, value, exported, readonly, conditional, scope.
Every umask assignment - path, line, value, symbolic, conditional, scope.
The winning PATH assignment for root, verbatim, with its file and line.
Each root PATH element - position, value, exists, mode, uid, gid, group_writable, world_writable, is_dot, variable, unresolved, undeclared.
World-writable files found by the deep walk, with path, sticky, uid, gid, package_declared.
Whether the deep walk finished within its budget.
Every cron/at configuration and spool file - path, scope, user, mode, owner and the group/other-writable flags.
The cron and at directories - path, mode, owner and the group/other-writable flags.
The systemd timer unit-file inventory - name and enablement state.
